claim: Skills load only name and description at startup (~100 tokens per skill); body loads on demand when Claude decides the skill is relevant.
quote: Create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with /skill-name... unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when it's used.

claim: Enterprise deployments average ~$13/dev/active day and $150–250/dev/month; MCP tool definitions are deferred by default; rate limits scale with team size.
quote: Across enterprise deployments, the average cost is around $13 per developer per active day and $150-250 per developer per month, with costs remaining below $30 per active day for 90% of users.

claim: Per-server MCP token measurements: Playwright 3,442 tokens, Gmail 2,640 tokens, Jira ~17,000 tokens, GitHub MCP 8k–12k; a 5-server setup can consume 50k–66k tokens before first prompt.
quote: Playwright: ~3,442 tokens (22 tools). Gmail: ~2,640 tokens (7 tools). Individual tools vary dramatically—the most expensive single Gmail tool (gmail_create_draft) costs 820 tokens alone.

claim: A single Skill consumes roughly 30–50 tokens until invoked; teams routinely run 20–50 Skills simultaneously with negligible overhead; root cause of non-triggering skills is almost always the description field.
quote: MCP is connectivity, Skills are procedural knowledge... A single Skill consumes roughly 30-50 tokens until invoked through progressive disclosure. However, a five-server MCP setup with typical tooling costs approximately 55,000 tokens upfront.

claim: The description field is the primary mechanism Claude uses to decide whether to load a skill; must include both what and when; always write in third person; max 1024 characters.
quote: The description field enables Skill discovery and should include both what the Skill does and when to use it... Always write in third person. The description is injected into the system prompt, and inconsistent point-of-view can cause discovery problems.

claim: MCP defines six primitives: server-side tools, resources, and prompts; client-side sampling, roots, and elicitation.
quote: The current MCP specification defines an open protocol for connecting LLM applications with external data sources and tools, using a host-client-server architecture and primitives such as tools, resources, prompts, sampling, roots, and elicitation.

claim: MCP sampling adds 200–800ms per call; best for classification and validation, not for voice pipelines needing <300ms; check clientCapabilities before using elicitation.
quote: Adds 200-800ms per call. Worth the cost for classification and validation; skip it for sub-100ms decisions or voice pipelines requiring 'sub-300ms voice response' latency.

claim: claude -p --bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and CLAUDE.md; is the recommended mode for CI/CD; stdin capped at 10MB.
quote: Add --bare to reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md... --bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release.

claim: The Agent SDK gives the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code in Python and TypeScript; starting June 15 2026 usage moves to a separate monthly credit.
quote: Build AI agents that autonomously read files, run commands, search the web, edit code, and more. The Agent SDK gives you the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code, programmable in Python and TypeScript.

claim: Claude Agent SDK Python package on GitHub.
quote: Python SDK for the Claude Agent SDK.

claim: Claude Agent SDK TypeScript package on GitHub; bundles a native Claude Code binary so separate installation is not required.
quote: The TypeScript SDK bundles a native Claude Code binary for your platform as an optional dependency, so you don't need to install Claude Code separately.

claim: 2026 MCP roadmap prioritises stateless horizontal scaling via HTTP transport evolution and .well-known capability discovery; Tasks primitive for agent-to-agent communication; governance via Working Groups.
quote: The roadmap emphasizes enabling servers to 'scale horizontally without having to hold state.' Key improvements include evolving the HTTP transport and session model for stateless operation, implementing a standard metadata format via .well-known.

claim: MCP production targets: >1,000 req/s per instance, P95 <100ms, P99 <500ms, error rate <0.1%, >99.9% uptime; use single-responsibility servers with strict schemas.
quote: Throughput: >1000 requests/second per instance. P95 latency: <100ms (simple operations). P99 latency: <500ms (complex operations). Error rate: <0.1%. Availability: >99.9% uptime.

claim: Community registry of MCP server implementations.
quote: Reference implementations and community servers for the Model Context Protocol.

claim: MCP Tool Search (Jan 2026) auto-enables when tool definitions exceed 10% of context window, delivering up to 95% reduction in startup token cost; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto:5 lowers threshold to 5%.
quote: As of January 2026, MCP Tool Search auto-enables when tool definitions exceed 10% of your context window... Users with many MCP servers report up to 95% reduction in startup token cost.

claim: Enterprise MCP deployments use a gateway pattern for centralized auth, routing, and policy enforcement; OAuth 2.1 re-authentication per tool call; isolated virtual servers per team with separate audit trails.
quote: Organizations should implement re-authenticating on each tool call rather than relying on a session-level token that could be hijacked or misused. The hardening phase explicitly introduces OAuth2 authentication, centralized secrets management, clear tool schemas, and an MCP Gateway.
